newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Students decry Cambodian king's amnesty plan.
newsitem.headline: Students decry Cambodian king's amnesty plan.

text.p: University students have petitioned King Norodom Sihanouk to reverse his recent call for amnesty for most of Cambodia's prisoners.

The students, in a statement released on Thursday, wrote that the king's proposal to release all but the most dangerous criminals would create anarchy in the streets and encourage Cambodians to commit more murders, theft and terrorism.
"We are worried about the security and safety of the people of Cambodia after the royal decree of your majesty to release prisoners in the jails," read the petition.
It was signed by students who said they represented Phnom Penh University and the faculties of agriculture, fine arts, technology, engineering and medicine.
Last week the king proposed the release of all but the most hardened criminals to mark his 74th birthday on October 31 in light of pardons given to Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
Sihanouk, who is empowered by the constitution to grant amnesty, said others who had committed far lesser crimes than the Khmer Rouge should be forgiven.

The king pardoned dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary last month from a 1979 death sentence for the rebel's role in the genocide of more than one million people during the 1975-1979 rule of Pol Pot.
Ieng Sary, foreign minister under Khmer Rouge rule, broke with Pol Pot in August and has been negotiating peace with the government.

Since the king's announcement, Prince Norodom Sirivudh, who was exiled last year over an alleged plot to kill Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, has written to Sihanouk asking for permission to return home from France.
The students, however, wrote in their petition that Sirivudh should not be granted an amnesty.
Aid workers estimated there are 2,000 prisoners in Cambodia, which has a population of 10.5 million.
